source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus carries 44 MW of IT capacity across three buildings, ranking 12th among the 25 Virginia facilities that publish power figures and amounting to 2.7% of the state's 1,603 MW announced total.

Virginia maps 330 data center facilities and only 25 of them publish a power figure. Every rank and share computed from those figures describes a minority of the state's capacity, so Sterling's 2.7% is a share of what operators disclose rather than of what Virginia has built. The published total is the countable part of the market, not the whole of it.

For AI the relevant question is racks and power per rack. At 40 kW per rack, 44 MW implies roughly 1,100 racks, which is a meaningful amount of training or inference floor space. The certifications cover financial, healthcare, federal, and information security workloads, which shows the campus was built for regulated tenants rather than for any one compute buyer.

What the data does not say is who occupies the space, how much of the 44 MW is energized, or whether any of it serves AI. The record also carries no announced expansion, which the suitability score of 70 lists as its missing input. A mid-tier state rank can still be a large facility in absolute terms, and a campus with no published expansion may be either full or holding room.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
